tables.description: Precomputed, for picking a night: one row per HEADLINE show that has a setlist. A run is consecutive nights by one act at one venue (a one-night show is a run of 1).

columns.name: show_id
columns.description: The unique identifier for a specific concert show.

columns.name: artist_mbid
columns.description: The MusicBrainz identifier for the artist performing at the show run.

columns.name: artist_name
columns.description: The name of the artist performing at the show run.

columns.name: venue_name
columns.description: The name of the venue where the concert show took place.

columns.name: show_date
columns.description: The calendar date when the concert show occurred.

columns.name: tour_name
columns.description: The name of the concert tour associated with the show run.

columns.name: run_start
columns.description: Date of the first night of this run.

columns.name: run_size
columns.description: How many nights are in the run (1 = a single show).

columns.name: night_no
columns.description: Which night of the run this is (1 = first).

columns.name: guest_songs
columns.description: Songs on this night where setlist.fm lists a guest.

columns.name: debut_songs
columns.description: Songs whose fan note says debut, surprise, first performance, first time or mashup.

columns.name: one_night_songs
columns.description: Songs played on this night and no other night of the run. NULL when run_size = 1.

tables.description: One act's performance at one venue on one date, from setlist.fm (2022-2025). Openers and festival acts get their own rows.

columns.name: show_id
columns.description: setlist.fm setlist id. Join key to songs_played.show_id.

columns.name: show_date
columns.description: Date of the show. No start time is available.

columns.name: venue_id
columns.description: The unique identifier for the concert venue.

columns.name: artist_mbid
columns.description: MusicBrainz artist id. Filter on this, not artist_name.

columns.name: artist_name
columns.description: Artist name as on setlist.fm. Use find_names to get the exact spelling.

columns.name: tour_name
columns.description: The name of the concert tour for the scheduled show.

columns.name: n_songs
columns.description: Songs performed live (tape intros excluded). 0 means fans never logged the setlist.

columns.name: role
columns.description: headliner, support, festival (6+ acts logged that night: festivals, benefit and tribute shows), cameo (the only act logged at an arena/stadium that night, 1-6 songs: anthems, halftime sets), or unknown (no setlist).

columns.name: acts_that_night
columns.description: How many acts setlist.fm logged at this venue on this date.

columns.name: show_note
columns.description: Free-text note from the fan who logged it, e.g. 'Approximate order'.

columns.name: setlistfm_url
columns.description: The source URL of the setlist on setlist.fm.

tables.description: One song performed at one show, in order. Tape intros are excluded.

columns.name: show_id
columns.description: The unique identifier of the concert show where the song was played.

columns.name: position
columns.description: 1-based order in the show, across all sets.

columns.name: song_name
columns.description: The title of the song performed during the concert setlist.

columns.name: is_encore
columns.description: A boolean indicating whether the song was performed as part of the encore.

columns.name: is_cover
columns.description: True if the artist played someone else's song. original_artist says whose.

columns.name: original_artist
columns.description: The original artist of the song if it was a cover performance.

columns.name: guest
columns.description: A guest who joined for this song (surprise guests), else NULL.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Fan note on the song, e.g. 'Acoustic', 'snippet', 'with string section'.

columns.name: is_partial
columns.description: True when the note says snippet/tease/intro/partial. Exclude these when counting 'played the hit'.

columns.name: chart_title
columns.description: The Hot 100 title this song matched, or NULL if it never charted for the credited artist.

columns.name: chart_performer
columns.description: The Billboard credit string of the matched song.

columns.name: chart_peak
columns.description: Best Hot 100 position of the matched song (1 = #1).

columns.name: chart_first_week
columns.description: First week the matched song was on the Hot 100.

columns.name: chart_last_week
columns.description: Last week the matched song was on the Hot 100.

columns.name: is_own_hit
columns.description: True if the artist played their OWN Hot 100 song (not a cover).

tables.description: One NYC-area venue we track (21 total: 20 in NYC plus MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ).

columns.name: venue_id
columns.description: setlist.fm venue id. Join key to shows.venue_id.

columns.name: venue_name
columns.description: The name of the concert venue in New York City.

columns.name: aliases
columns.description: Nicknames people use, semicolon-separated ('MSG; the Garden').

columns.name: borough
columns.description: The New York City borough where the venue is located.

columns.name: capacity
columns.description: Approximate capacity, hand-entered. Not attendance.

columns.name: size_tier
columns.description: club (<=2,000), mid-size, or arena/stadium (>=13,000). Used for the venue ladder.

notes: Filter artists by artist_mbid from find_names, never by artist_name = '...'.
Count a 'concert' only where shows.role = 'headliner' unless the user asks about openers or festivals.
Exclude is_partial songs when counting whether a song was played.
A 'hit' means a Hot 100 song (songs_played.chart_title IS NOT NULL). Billboard is US-only and singles-only.
To list an artist's hits they did NOT play: artist_chart_credits -> chart_songs, anti-join songs_played.
The Hot 100 runs past 2025 but setlists stop at 2025: only count songs that first charted before the show date.

PICK A NIGHT: for 'which night should I go to' or 'best night' questions, query run_nights and show guest_songs, debut_songs and one_night_songs side by side for each night, with no single score. Always also say: (1) venue context, the share of run_nights rows at that venue with guest_songs > 0, e.g. 'MetLife shows had a guest 47% of the time'; (2) how many nights you compared; (3) that last nights are not reliably more surprising than other nights; (4) that the data cannot see future lineups, so any odds are only how often it happened before.
limits: Only 21 NYC-area venues, 2022-2025 (20 in NYC plus MetLife Stadium in New Jersey). No other cities, years, or venues (no UBS Arena, Prudential Center).
No ticket prices, attendance, start times, reviews, or streaming numbers.
setlist.fm is fan-logged: about a third of shows have no setlist and order is sometimes approximate.
Song matching is by normalized title + artist; medleys and retitled songs can be missed.
Guests and debuts come from fan notes, so an unlogged surprise counts as zero. The data only has past shows: it can say how often surprises happened before, never what a future night will have.
